title: Soft Serve blended with candy or cookies

content.title: About
content.content: Soft‑serve is a light, aerated frozen dessert served in swirls. The version blended with candy or cookies combines a creamy vanilla‑based base with finely chopped sweets, creating crunchy bits and extra flavor throughout the swirl.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft‑serve originated in the United States in the 1930s and quickly became a fast‑food staple.
Candies or cookie pieces are folded in at the end of the whipping process to preserve their texture.
In some regions local treats are used – for example, gingerbread crumbs or caramel drops.
Soft‑serve is served at about –6 °C, making it softer than regular ice cream.
Vegan versions can be made with plant‑based milks and oils.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk contributes riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: Soft‑serve typically contains less fat than traditional ice cream, making it a lighter option when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Added candies or cookies supply simple sugars that rapidly replenish blood glucose after activity.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Sweet desserts stimulate serotonin production, which can improve mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The extra sweets raise the overall sugar level, which can be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Cookies may contain nuts, gluten, or dairy, triggering allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite lower fat, the added candies make the dessert relatively high in calories.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Traditional soft‑serve contains lactose; those who are intolerant should choose a lactose‑free version.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve soft‑serve in a cone or cup immediately after it’s made while it’s still airy. Sprinkle candy pieces, chocolate chips, or cookie crumbs on top for extra crunch. It pairs well with fruit sauces or fresh berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Consume soft‑serve within 30–60 minutes of preparation, as it will harden over time. If you must store it, keep it in a sealed container in a freezer at –18 °C for no more than 24 hours.
